notes: Fresh check for the IGME Spain lithium slice (8 Nov 2026). Not part of the gate.

questions.q: Where are the highest lithium values in Spanish stream sediments? Show them on a map.

truth.n: SELECT count(*) FROM geochem.sample_chemistry_wide WHERE source_system='SPAIN_IGME_GEOCHEMISTRY' AND sample_type_name='Stream Sediment' AND li_t IS NOT NULL

questions.judge: Uses the IGME Spain data (SPAIN_IGME_GEOCHEMISTRY) stream sediments (about 21,000 with Li from the Mapa Geoquímico de España and Badajoz Sur plus FOREGS), shows the highest Li values on a map (top values around 200-310 ppm), names the campaign(s), says these are stream-sediment values (not ore grades), mentions the method/detection limit or that methods differ by campaign, and credits IGME as 'Source: © NC Geological Survey of Spain (IGME)' or equivalent without implying endorsement. Does not mix in the 86 water values.

questions.q: Do you have nickel geochemistry for Spain?
questions.judge: Says no: only lithium and copper have been loaded so far from IGME's Spanish geochemistry; nickel is not loaded yet (IGME holds it). Must not claim Spanish nickel analyses exist in the database.

questions.q: Where are the strongest copper anomalies in Spanish stream sediments? Show them on a map.
questions.judge: Uses IGME Spain copper (SPAIN_IGME_GEOCHEMISTRY) stream sediments, shows the highest values or anomalous cells on a map, places them in campaigns or named regions (campaign names OR regions such as the Iberian Pyrite Belt / Badajoz / Guadalupe area are fine), says detection limits/methods differ by campaign or that old campaigns are coarser, says the Badajoz panned heavy-mineral concentrates were left out or kept separate (e.g. by filtering to stream sediments), says these are sediment values not ore grades, and credits IGME (IGME's own required wording 'Source: © NC Geological Survey of Spain (IGME)' is correct) without implying endorsement.
